text.p: International Business Machines Corp Tuesday said it plans to spend $440 million to expand disk drive and component manufacturing in Asia, Europe and North America.
IBM said the investment, combined with previous investments in its Storage Systems Division announced in March and July, bring the total invested in its storage business to $1.32 billion.
The Storage Systems Division has facilities in Germany, Hungary, Singapore, Japan, China, Mexico, the United States, and, with Tuesday's announcement, Thailand.

IBM said a portion of the $440 million investment is designated for a new disk drive manufacturing facility in Prachinburi, about 90 miles from Bangkok. Construction is expected to begin early next year, with disk drives coming off the line by the first quarter of 1998.
IBM said the Prachinburi facility will handle final assembly and testing of IBM's high-performance, high-capacity, 2.5-inch disk drives for the mobile storage business.

IBM said the $440 million also includes additional investment in hard disk drive technology component manufacturing capacity in San Jose, Calif. New manufacturing lines will come on line there in 1997 and 1998.

IBM said the Storage Systems Division facility in Mainz, Germany, has received additional funding this year to increase manufacturing capacity for technology disk drive components, primarily for the European market.
